movement_source: row 'Total impairment (charges)/benefits', column Full Year Sept 2024 -> column Full Year Sept 2025
headline: WBC's credit impairment charge fell $113m (21%) to $424m in FY25 from $537m in FY24, equal to 5bps of average gross loans versus 7bps (ev-1, ev-41, ev-42, ev-9, ev-35). The charge is identical on statutory and ex-Notable-Items bases (ev-43, ev-44), so no basis disagreement arises. The bank attributes the fall "mainly due to an increase in write-backs and recoveries partly offset by a higher CAP charge" (ev-10); page 9 adds "a reduction in new IAPs and higher write-backs and recoveries... partly offset by an increase for new portfolio overlays" (ev-42). The impairment note's provision-type rows bridge the movement exactly: write-backs -102, recoveries -57, new IAPs -15, other changes in CAPs -14, offset by higher CAP write-offs +75 (ev-2 to ev-7). The pack's FY24-FY25 net profit walk independently prints an impairment charges bar of +$113m to profit (ev-30). Net write-offs to average gross loans rose 5bps to 6bps (ev-19).

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 less Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Write-backs more than doubled to $195m from $93m, +110% (ev-3), the single largest benefit. The bank says they were "mostly in the wholesale & retail trade and manufacturing sectors" (ev-18) and names "an increase in write-backs and recoveries" as the main reason the charge fell (ev-10). In New Zealand the benefit was "driven by write-backs and a CAP benefit, largely in the mortgages portfolio" (ev-28).

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 less Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Recoveries rose 30% to $247m from $190m (ev-4), "mostly within the credit cards and personal loan portfolios" (ev-17). The pack labels this driver "Higher Cards & Personal Loans recoveries" (ev-45). This is the mirror of the higher cards/personal-loan write-offs: gross write-offs rose while recoveries against them also rose, so net write-offs to average gross loans still increased 1bp to 6bps (ev-19).

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 less Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: New IAPs fell 4% to $408m from $423m (ev-2), "mostly in the services and wholesale & retail trade sectors and the mortgages portfolio" (ev-16). Institutional drove this: an impairment benefit of $1m against a $120m charge in FY24 (a -$121m swing), "driven by revisions to economic forecasts partly offset by new IAPs within the service sector" (ev-25, ev-20, ev-21). Business & Wealth's charge conversely reflects "new IAPs in the wholesale & retail trade sector" (ev-23). Total IAPs, write-backs and recoveries swung to a $34m benefit from a $140m charge (ev-5).

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 less Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: CAP write-offs rose 15% to $561m from $486m (ev-6), the main offset — the bank's "higher CAP charge" (ev-10); total CAPs rose 15% to $458m from $397m (ev-8). Write-offs were "largely within the credit card and personal loan portfolios" (ev-11). Consumer's charge of $217m (from $248m) "reflects write-offs in cards and personal lending", at 4bps of average loans, down 1bp (ev-26, ev-20, ev-21).

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 less Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: A net benefit of $103m versus $89m, +16% (ev-7) — a small net number hiding large offsetting parts. Benefits: "an improved economic outlook for commercial property prices and interest rates" (ev-12) and mortgage 90+ day delinquencies falling from 1.05% to 0.70% (ev-13). Offsets: a 5ppt rise in the downside scenario weight "reflecting a rise in geopolitical instability" (ev-14) and "an increase for new portfolio overlays" (ev-15, ev-42). Balance context: modelled CAPs fell $168m while overlays rose $59m to $238m (ev-37, ev-36, ev-39). Business & Wealth's charge rose to 23bps of average loans from 14bps on "higher overlays, an increase in the downside scenario" (ev-23).

notable_items: Impairment (charges)/benefits carry no Notable Items adjustment: (424) statutory equals (424) ex Notable Items in FY25, and (537) equals (537) in FY24 (ev-43, ev-44).

disagreements.topic: New Zealand FY25 impairment benefit: $41m vs $44m
values: $44m (New Zealand segment commentary, results announcement p45)
disagreements.explanation: The A$-equivalent segment table prints a $41m NZ impairment benefit (ev-20), which is the figure that sums to the Group's $424m charge; the New Zealand section commentary states a $44m benefit (ev-29) on a NZ$ basis. The A$ figure is the one consistent with the Group bridge.

The bank states "1H25 has been restated for the above changes. FY24 has not been revised" (ev-22), including transfer of merchant services from Business & Wealth to Institutional and auto finance to Group Businesses. Divisional impairment deltas therefore mix real credit movements with composition shifts, so the where-layer is narrative only and the quantified bridge is taken from the provision-type rows.

limitations: The divisional where-layer deltas are computed by me from the two period columns (FY25 less FY24, ev-20/ev-21): Consumer -31 (217 vs 248), Business & Wealth +103 (245 vs 142), Institutional -121 (benefit of 1 vs charge of 120), New Zealand -66 (benefit of 41 vs charge of 25), Group Businesses +2 (4 vs 2); these sum to -113. The bank does not print a divisional change column for impairment, and FY24 divisional comparatives are not restated for FY25 segment composition changes (ev-22), so these divisional deltas are less reliable than the provision-type bridge.

The bank publishes no FY24-to-FY25 waterfall of the impairment charge itself. The pack's IMPAIRMENT CHARGES COMPOSITION chart (p49) is on a 2H24/1H25/2H25 half basis and is context only; the only primary-comparison chart is the net profit walk (ev-30), which prints impairment as a single +$113m bar with no further decomposition.

'Other changes in CAPs' (-$14m) is a net bar spanning opposing forces the bank names but does not individually quantify in the charge: improved commercial property price and interest rate outlook and lower mortgage delinquencies against a 5ppt downside scenario weight increase and new portfolio overlays (ev-12 to ev-15). The $168m modelled CAP decrease and $59m overlay increase (ev-37, ev-36) are provision-BALANCE movements, not components of the period charge.

The collective-provision movement cannot be split between portfolio volume growth and risk migration from the disclosure available; no evidence supports a collective.volume or collective.asset_quality contribution, so neither is claimed.

The loss rate denominators differ slightly by page: p21 prints 'Impairment charges/(benefits) to average loans' (5bps vs 7bps, ev-9) while p9 says '5 basis points of average gross loans' (ev-42); the pack labels it 'Impairment charges to average loans annualised' (ev-35). All give the same 2bps improvement.
Basis normalised from 'cash' to 'ex_notables': no page in evidence prints 'cash' beside the movement, and the registry names ex_notables as the bank's headline basis.

Capped at 80: write_backs_recoveries -102 $m, write_backs_recoveries -57 $m, individual_provisions -15 $m, write_offs_direct +75 $m, overlays_fla -14 $m. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
